Requires ID confirmation: Possible Hawksbill Turtle (Eretmochelys imbricata) Temperature approx. 40deg.C, sunny – sun setting, dry, slightly windy, wind direction from the sea coming East-West to land, and ‘choppy’ waves. Sandy beach, with open Gulf waters. South of usual turtle nesting grounds. Found washed up on shoreline, upside down and dead, decomposing had begun (odour close to it) but not so visibly advanced. Stomach looks cut open. Size: approx. 1.5m length, beak to tail. No visible ID tag. Photos show animal body against human adult (1.76m height) and animal head against human hand (12cm length)
